goal: Ship the Import offer: create it at the subscribe+connect junction, let the owner accept or decline it once per location, and enqueue the Review import only on Yes — so no import runs without Import consent (D1/D9).
non_goals: No migration — the Import consent columns shipped as migrations 100+101 (#673). The one-migration-in-flight slot stays free.
No reviews list, no unanswered-first sort, no per-row Generate/Regenerate — that is #678. Imported reviews surface only through the existing dashboard recentReviews feed.
No worker-side consent guard in ZernioBackfillWorker — that is #679. This ticket ships the writer and two enqueue gates; #679 adds the fail-closed run-time chokepoint.
No gate on archive-location-tx.ts reactivation catch-up — the third §5 enqueue path stays with #676.
No stored 'expired' value, no poller, no lazy write-back, no expiry notification — expiry is derived on read (spec §5.3, #670).
No feature flag and no env-vars.md entry (ADR 0015 R1). Ordering carries the rollout; backout is git revert.
No permanent import affordance in settings (spec §8, rejected at design).
No changes to the live-ingest lane. A declined location keeps receiving live-lane drafts for new reviews — that is what the reassurance line promises.

No typed job_outbox helper for ZERNIO_INITIAL_BACKFILL — the topic has none today and finalize-tx.ts enqueues raw; minting one would turn every raw site red under ci:outbox-seam and force migrating them in this PR (invariant #2's explicit carve-out).
No rename of the zernio_initial_backfill topic or zernio_backfill_runs table (map #667, out of scope).
user_visible_behavior: When a location reaches the subscribe+connect junction — whichever of subscription activation and Google connection lands second — an Import offer is created with a deadline 7 days out, and the dashboard shows the Import offer banner for the location currently in scope.

The banner reads: 'Import your recent reviews?' / 'We can pull in your 100 most recent Google reviews from the past year so you can generate replies for them. Nothing gets posted — you choose what to reply to.' / 'This is a one-time import, available for the next 7 days. New reviews will still be handled automatically either way.' with actions 'Import my reviews' and 'No thanks'.
Clicking 'Import my reviews' records the acceptance and enqueues the Review import in one transaction; the click returns immediately and never blocks on Zernio.

After accepting, the banner shows 'Importing your reviews… this usually takes a minute', then resolves to 'Imported N reviews. They're in your reviews list.' — or 'No recent reviews found — nothing to import.' when the import stored zero.
Clicking 'No thanks' records the decline and the banner disappears permanently for that location. Nothing is fetched from Zernio and no import is ever enqueued.
An owner who answers after the 7-day deadline gets no write and no import — the banner is already gone, and a late request is rejected.

Connecting Google no longer starts an import on its own: the junction creates the offer, and the import is enqueued only by an acceptance (or resumed for a location that already accepted and whose import never completed).
A past_due → active recovery no longer re-imports for a location that declined the offer (the §5.2 bug).
Re-adding a location whose archived row for the same Google place had declined or let the offer expire does not re-offer the import — the new row inherits that decision.
invariants: Invariant #2 (transactional outbox): the acceptance write and the zernio_initial_backfill enqueue happen in ONE Postgres transaction. Raw INSERT INTO job_outbox, matching finalize-tx.ts — the topic has no helper.
Invariant #1 (Vercel = UI only): the decision route performs Postgres writes only. No Zernio call, no LLM call, no long-running work in Next.js — the fetch is the worker's job (D9).
Invariant #8 (auth scope): every read and write is scoped by account_id and business_id; the decision route resolves its location from owner scope and never trusts a client-supplied business id.
Invariant #15: import-consent.ts takes its db client as an explicit sql/tx parameter and never imports @/lib/db/server. Only the route and the ingress composition roots import the singleton.
Invariant #13 / ADR 0015 R1: no feature flag, no NEXT_PUBLIC_ companion, no env-vars.md entry.

F3 atomic transition contract (#673 adversarial review, shared with #679): acceptance and decline UPDATE only rows that are pending AND unexpired, guarded by the UPDATE's WHERE predicate rather than read-then-write. A terminal state — accepted or declined — is never overwritten by any path.

One owner for the derivation: importConsentStateSql is the single place 'pending AND import_offer_expires_at <= now()' is spelled. The banner, the decision route, the two enqueue gates, and (after rebase) #679's worker guard all consult it.
D9: nothing is fetched from Zernio before an acceptance is recorded. D2: the enqueued topic is zernio_initial_backfill, never generate_response — the import writes no replies.
Expiry is evaluated by Postgres now(), never a JS Date, so the timestamptz microsecond-truncation class cannot apply at the boundary.
D8 permanence: no path resurrects a declined or derived-expired offer — including re-add of an archived location and a repeated junction.
edge_cases: Junction fires twice (reconnect, or activation after connect) → createImportOffer is idempotent: it stamps only a pending row with a NULL deadline, so the 7-day clock is never extended or restarted.
Junction reached with subscription_activated_at NULL → no offer is created; the existing finalize-tx warn branch is unchanged.

Late click — the owner answers at or after the deadline → the UPDATE matches zero rows and the route returns a gone/conflict outcome with no write and no enqueue. The <= boundary is inclusive, per §5.3's predicate verbatim.
Double-click or duplicate POST of accept → the second UPDATE matches zero rows (already accepted); the route is idempotent and exactly one import is enqueued.
Accept then decline (racing tabs) → whichever transition commits first wins; the second matches zero rows. No terminal state is overwritten.

Offer accepted but the import never completes (Zernio outage, worker crash) → consent stays accepted, zernio_backfill_runs.completed_at stays NULL, and §5.1 retryability is preserved. The banner shows the importing state.

The import's outbox row reaches a terminal non-completed status → the banner reports a failed import rather than spinning forever (draft-status precedent maps every terminal non-completed status to failed).
Import completes having stored zero reviews (no reviews inside the Import window) → success, not an error: 'No recent reviews found — nothing to import.' (spec §7).
Multi-location account → the offer, the decision, and the banner are per location; the banner shows the offer for the location currently in scope and switching scope surfaces the next one.

Re-adding an archived location for the same google_place_id → the new businesses row inherits the archived sibling's import_decision / _at / _expires_at, so a declined or expired offer is never re-offered (F3 constraint 1).
Owner never opens the dashboard → the deadline still passes; the offer derives expired and is never shown. Nothing is imported (the fail-closed direction).
A declined location keeps receiving live-lane drafts for new reviews — declining the import is not declining the product.
Reviews already ingested live are deduped by importReview's ON CONFLICT, so an accepted import after a period of live ingestion cannot duplicate rows.

src/app/api/dashboard/past-replies/draft-status/route.ts — GET polling route: no CSRF wrapper, tenant-ownership guard on the resolved row, and the discriminated status union where every terminal non-completed outbox status maps to failed.

rollback_plan: git revert the PR (ADR 0015 R1 — no flag exists to flip). No migration rides this ticket, so there is no schema state to undo; the Import consent columns stay and revert to being written by nobody. Reverting restores the unconditional junction enqueue, which is inert in both environments while prod and staging hold zero businesses. Order: revert, redeploy the Railway worker (ingress change), redeploy Vercel (route + banner). Any import_decision rows written before the revert stay on the row and are re-honoured when the PR re-lands — the record is never rewritten.
observability: Analytics events on the decision tx, enqueued via enqueueAnalyticsEvent alongside the state change (the gbp_connected precedent in finalize-tx.ts): import_offer_created at the junction, and import_decision_recorded carrying accepted or declined. Their ratio is the churn signal the reassurance line exists to protect — a decline rate climbing is the one number that says the copy is failing.

A structured log line from the decision route on a rejected late click, naming the derived consent state and business_id, so 'the owner says the button did nothing' resolves to an expiry rather than an outage.

Counter-signal for the silent failure: an accepted import whose zernio_backfill_runs row still has completed_at NULL well past the run window means the import stalled — the same shape the existing skip reasons produce, queryable in Railway logs alongside the run row.
No new metric or Sentry event: a decline and an expiry are expected outcomes, not errors, and paging on either would page on normal use.
